board.name: ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.49
board.variant_note: The "B" listing is the same board in Case B with a Li-Po battery.
board.source: Waveshare wiki (ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.49); Espressif ESP32-S3 datasheet for the CPU clock

revision.source: task 0.3, spikes/hw: the touch controller's interrupt reaches TCA9554 P0 (it pulsed low only while a finger was down, on each of three taps), and V1 boards have no touch interrupt. Inferred from that; the silkscreen wasn't read (the case can't be opened).

i2c.note: The main bus carries the expander, the codec, the microphone ADC, the RTC and the IMU. Touch has its own bus.
i2c.source: task 0.3, spikes/hw: pins from the Waveshare demo (facts only); a scan of the bus found ES8311 0x18, TCA9554 0x20, ES7210 0x40, PCF85063 0x51 and QMI8658 0x6B

expander.source: task 0.3, spikes/hw: the schematic (Waveshare wiki) names each port pin and routes the expander's INT to GPIO42; the bus scan found the chip at 0x20; P0 (touch interrupt), P5 (TE) and P7 (amplifier) were confirmed on the board

display.source: Waveshare wiki and demo repo (facts only; the repo has no licence). Full-frame-only and no hardware rotation: atomic14's AXS15231B write-up (community). PPI and mm computed from the 3.49-inch diagonal and 172x640.

rotation.source: task 0.3, spikes/hw: with cw90 the image is upright when the edge with the buttons is at the top (owner)

flush_ms.source: task 0.3, spikes/hw: mean of 100 full-frame flushes, 13.0 ms (p95 13.2), QSPI at 40 MHz, rotating 64-row strips into two internal bounce buffers while the previous strip is sent. Rotating the whole frame first (the kit's lcd349__rotate_frame, PSRAM to PSRAM) took 75.7 ms, so the hardware backend must rotate in strips.

refresh_hz.source: task 0.3, spikes/hw: the panel's TE signal (expander P5) pulses every 16.41 ms (15-18 ms) over 1,218 pulses (spikes/hw/logs/expander-and-tone.log)

backlight_active_low.source: task 0.3, spikes/hw: the Waveshare demo drives duty 0 for full brightness (facts only); confirmed on the board with an inverted 50 kHz PWM output

case.name: Case B
case.source: Waveshare wiki (Case B dimensions); the owner confirmed the board is in Case B

screen_offset_mm.source: task 0.3: Waveshare's Case B dimension drawing (case 98.50 x 34.80 mm, active area 84.00 x 22.58 mm), margins scaled from the drawing (about 0.5 mm), turned 180 degrees to the upright landscape (buttons edge at the top)

int_pin.V2: TCA9554 P0 (unusable: the expander's interrupt on GPIO42 fires on every input change, including TE on P5)

touch.source: Waveshare wiki and demo repo (facts only); the controller reports up to two points (multi_point), and the kit uses the first

period_ms.source: task 0.3, spikes/hw: a finger held still, 4 s per period. The controller makes a new report about every 16.8 ms and answers 'no new data' (0x30 in every byte) between reports, which reads like a lift: 5 ms 224 false lifts, 10 ms 147, 15 ms 19, 20 ms and 30 ms none. 30 ms leaves headroom for scheduling jitter.

multi_point.source: task 0.3, spikes/hw: two fingers give a report with two points, each with a touch ID (the kit still uses one point)

through_case.source: task 0.3: Case B leaves the glass open; every touch test ran through the owner's screen protector

buttons.source: Waveshare wiki and demo repo (facts only); Espressif ESP32-S3 boot-mode strapping for GPIO0

items.reset_trap: Held through a reset, BOOT enters the ROM download mode, so never design a boot-time BOOT combination.

position_mm.source: task 0.3: Waveshare's Case B drawing and photos. The buttons are 10 mm apart on the top edge (upright landscape), at the right-hand end by the USB-C port, BOOT nearest it (layout confirmed by the owner); the centre is scaled from the drawing (about 0.5 mm); y is the case edge.

task 0.3: Waveshare's Case B drawing and photos. PWR is the middle of the three buttons at the right-hand end of the top edge (upright landscape; layout confirmed by the owner); the centre is scaled from the drawing (about 0.5 mm); y is the case edge.

hold.note: On battery the board stays on only while P6 is asserted; releasing it powers the board off.

power.source: Waveshare wiki and demo repo (facts only); Case B battery confirmed by the owner

battery_capacity_mah.source: the cell's label, read by the owner: 2,500 mAh at 3.7 V, 9.25 Wh, rated 35 A

battery_curve.source: a measured discharge curve of the Case B cell (after task 0.3)
battery_curve.assumed_basis: a generic single-cell Li-Po open-circuit table (millivolts, percent)

power_states.what: Running with the backlight on and Wi-Fi connected

current_ma.source: task 0.3 (10 min average at USB 5 V, battery disconnected)

power_states.what: Backlight off, Wi-Fi connected and idle

current_ma.source: task 0.3 (10 min average at USB 5 V, battery disconnected)

power_states.what: Light sleep with modem power save, woken by BOOT or PWR

current_ma.source: task 0.3 (10 min average at USB 5 V, battery disconnected)

power_states.what: Power hold released on battery; the board is off
ROM download mode (BOOT held through a reset); the product does not run

audio.speaker: MX1.25 speaker header (a buyer review says a speaker is included)

codec.source: task 0.3, spikes/hw: the I2S pins from the schematic and Waveshare's codec configuration (facts only); the bus scan found the codec at 0x18, and the tones played through these pins were heard (owner)

amp_enable.value: TCA9554 P7, output, high = amplifier on
amp_enable.source: task 0.3: the schematic names P7 NS_MODE, the NS4150B amplifier's control pin (pulled down); Waveshare's demos set it high before playing. Confirmed by sound in spikes/hw: a tone with P7 high was heard, the same tone with P7 low wasn't.

speaker_connected.source: task 0.3, spikes/hw: tones through the ES8311 and NS4150B were heard (owner)

wifi.note: The ESP32-S3 has no 5 GHz radio. A phone hotspot must offer 2.4 GHz (iPhone: Maximize Compatibility).

kit.source: lcd349-kit design.md (kit behaviour, not a board fact)

internal_ram_kb.source: phase 1 task 10.3: the full board run of test_apps/board (go run ./tools/boardtest), the free internal heap after lcd349_init with every subsystem up, Wi-Fi included: 72,907 bytes on each of its four boots (heap_caps_get_free_size(MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL)); the largest free block was 31,744 bytes

lvgl_mem_kb.source: phase 1 task 10.3: LVGL 9.6.0's built-in heap in the board build, CONFIG_LV_MEM_SIZE=65536 bytes (LVGL's Kconfig default, which the kit and the examples keep) in test_apps/board's and examples/inputs' esp32s3 sdkconfig

fidelity_not_modelled.check_on_hardware: Time heavy work (parsing, crypto, big redraws) on the board; the emulator runs at host speed.
Check frame rates and large copies on the board.

fidelity_not_modelled.what: Radio behaviour (range, interference, roaming, real signal strength)
fidelity_not_modelled.check_on_hardware: Join your real networks, including a 2.4 GHz phone hotspot, and walk out of range.
Run on a low battery with Wi-Fi and audio active.

fidelity_not_modelled.what: Flash wear and NVS write limits
fidelity_not_modelled.check_on_hardware: Count storage writes per hour; avoid writing on every event.
Listen to every tone on the board, in the case.

fidelity_not_modelled.what: Touch feel: finger size, accuracy at the edges, touch through the case
fidelity_not_modelled.check_on_hardware: Use every touch target with a finger on the board, in the case.

fidelity_not_modelled.what: Task scheduling: one simulated core instead of two, host threads switched at the FreeRTOS tick, and the kit's own tasks at app_main's priority
fidelity_not_modelled.check_on_hardware: Test task priorities, timing races and core pinning on the board. In the emulator, avoid malloc and printf from tasks above priority 1 that share them with lower ones: a host lock can hang the instance.

fidelity_not_modelled.what: Network access follows the host, not the simulated Wi-Fi: sockets work even while the simulated station is disconnected
fidelity_not_modelled.check_on_hardware: Check that the product waits for LCD349_WIFI_CONNECTED before connecting, and recovers when Wi-Fi drops.

design_rules.why: 56 px is about 7.5 mm at 7.5 px/mm; smaller targets are missed by fingers.
design_rules.fix: Make the clickable object at least 56 x 56 px, or extend its click area; tag dense list rows "list-row".

design_rules.why: 12 px text is about 1.6 mm tall on this panel; smaller is unreadable at arm's length.
design_rules.fix: Use a font with a line height of at least 12 px.

design_rules.why: WCAG AA for normal text; small screens are read at a glance, often outdoors.
design_rules.fix: Darken the background or lighten the text until the ratio is at least 4.5:1 (checked on RGB565-quantised colours).

design_rules.why: Text that doesn't fit is cut off or runs outside its object.
design_rules.fix: Shorten the text, widen the object, or set a long mode (wrap, dots, or scroll).

design_rules.why: Characters missing from the font render as nothing or as boxes.
design_rules.fix: Use a font that contains every character shown, or replace the characters.

design_rules.why: Objects outside 640 x 172 are invisible on the device.
design_rules.fix: Move or resize the object to fit inside the screen.

design_rules.why: Overlapping click areas make a tap ambiguous.
design_rules.fix: Separate the clickable objects so their click areas don't intersect.

design_rules.why: Every frame is a full-frame flush, so kinetic scrolling judders.
design_rules.fix: Clear LV_OBJ_FLAG_SCROLL_MOMENTUM; page or step instead.
Use flat colours, or a gradient between close colours.
